  "screen_rationale": "The study quantitatively compares the predictive accuracy of different animal models (hERG vs. MICE) for human clinical outcomes (Torsade de Pointes), reporting concordance statistics like sensitivity, specificity, and AUC. It directly measures agreement between preclinical and clinical results.",
  "arm": "safety-pharmacology",
  "arm_evidence": "The study focuses on predicting Torsade de Pointes (TdP), a potentially lethal cardiac arrhythmia, which falls under cardiac safety pharmacology.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "cardiovascular"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study directly investigates cardiac arrhythmias (Torsade de Pointes) and ion channel block related to cardiovascular function.",
  "model_type": "in-vitro-or-in-silico-comparator",
  "model_evidence": "The study compares in vitro measurements of ion channel block (hERG, Cav1.2, Nav1.5) with clinical outcomes, using computational models (logistic regression) to predict human risk.",
  "species": [
    "mouse",
    "rat"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The study mentions using mice and rats in the context of drug development and testing, although the primary data is from in vitro assays. 'The human ether-à-go-go-related gene (hERG, Kv 11.1) channel has played an especially important role in cardiac safety... mice models: superior to the HERG model in predicting Torsade de Pointes.'",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study uses both hard outcomes (Torsade de Pointes, TdP) and biomarker-like measurements (IC50 values, ETPC Indexes, AUC, sensitivity, specificity) to assess predictive concordance."
